16 An escalator is 60 m long and lifts passengers through a vertical height of 30 m, as shown.
30 m
60 m
To drive the escalator against the forces of friction when there are no passengers requires a
power of 2.0 kW.
The escalator is used by passengers of average mass 60 kg and the power to overcome friction
remains constant.
How much power is required to drive the escalator when it is carrying 20 passengers and is
travelling at 0.75 m s–1?
A
4.4 kW
B
6.4 kW
C
8.8 kW
D
10.8 kW

hints: Notice the diagram gives both a $60\text{ m}$ slope length and a $30\text{ m}$ vertical height, so the $0.75\text{ m s}^{-1}$ along the escalator is not the vertical speed.
Recall power for lifting at constant speed is $P = Fv$ with $F$ equal to weight and $v$ the vertical component of velocity.
Calculate the vertical speed from the $30/60$ ratio, then find $mgv$ for $20 \times 60\text{ kg}$ and add the constant $2.0\text{ kW}$ for friction.
walkthrough: Total passenger mass is $m = 20 \times 60\text{ kg} = 1200\text{ kg}$, with weight $W = mg$.
The escalator speed $0.75\text{ m s}^{-1}$ is along the $60\text{ m}$ slope, while gravity acts through the $30\text{ m}$ vertical height.
Vertical component of velocity is $v_v = 0.75\text{ m s}^{-1} \times 30/60 = 0.375\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Power to lift passengers is rate of gain of potential energy: $P_{lift} = mgv_v = 1200 \times 9.81 \times 0.375 \approx 4415\text{ W} \approx 4.4\text{ kW}$.
Add the constant friction power: $P_{total} = 4.4\text{ kW} + 2.0\text{ kW} = 6.4\text{ kW}$. This is option B.

A.explanation: This is only the power to lift the passengers at $0.375\text{ m s}^{-1}$ vertically. It omits the constant $2.0\text{ kW}$ needed to overcome friction.

B.explanation: The sum of $2.0\text{ kW}$ for friction and about $4.4\text{ kW}$ to gain gravitational potential energy gives about $6.4\text{ kW}$.

C.explanation: This uses the $0.75\text{ m s}^{-1}$ slope speed as if it were the vertical speed, so it doubles the lifting power and also omits friction.

D.explanation: This uses the $0.75\text{ m s}^{-1}$ slope speed as the vertical speed to get about $8.8\text{ kW}$, then adds $2.0\text{ kW}$ for friction.
